title: How well do you know trans rights in Italy?
description: A technical quiz on Italian legislation: legal gender recognition, privacy, prisons, healthcare and discrimination.

questions.text: Since what year has it been possible to legally change one's sex in Italy?
questions.explanation: Law 164 of 14 April 1982 is the fundamental statute allowing the rectification of sex attribution in civil status records.

questions.text: Is surgery mandatory to obtain legal gender recognition in Italy?
options: Yes, it is always mandatory
No, since 2015 the Constitutional Court has ruled it is not a prerequisite
Only for trans women
Only if the judge requires it
questions.explanation: Constitutional Court ruling 221/2015 established that surgery is not a prerequisite but a possible choice. Ruling 180/2017 reaffirmed the principle, and ruling 143/2024 also removed the requirement of judicial authorization for those who choose surgery.

questions.text: After legal recognition, what happens to the birth certificate?
options: It is completely rewritten without any trace
The summary extract shows only the new data; the full one (with annotation) is accessible only by the person concerned
It remains unchanged with the original sex
It is deleted and replaced with a new one
questions.explanation: The summary extract — the document normally used — shows only the updated name and gender. The full extract contains the annotation of the court decision but can only be requested by the person themselves. Law enforcement can access the previous data for security reasons.

questions.text: What happens to the tax code (codice fiscale) after legal gender recognition?
options: It stays the same
Only the name changes but not the code
A completely new tax code is generated
A letter is added at the end
questions.explanation: The Italian tax code encodes gender in the date of birth (the day is increased by 40 for women). After rectification, the municipality automatically generates a new tax code consistent with the new gender.

questions.text: Is there a specific law in Italy regulating bathroom access for trans people?
options: Yes, Law 164/1982 also covers bathrooms
Yes, Legislative Decree 81/2008 sets precise rules
No, there is no specific national rule
Yes, but only in schools
questions.explanation: No Italian law specifically regulates bathroom access for transgender people. Legislative Decree 81/2008 on workplace safety requires separate bathrooms for men and women but does not address trans people. Some municipalities and universities have introduced gender-neutral bathrooms on a voluntary basis.

questions.text: On what basis does the Italian prison system assign trans people to a male or female prison?
options: The legal sex on identity documents
The gender identity declared by the person
Anatomical/genital sex, regardless of documents
A case-by-case decision by the supervising magistrate
questions.explanation: The DAP (Department of Prison Administration) uses anatomical-genital sex as the sole criterion. Even a trans woman with an F on her documents, if she has not undergone genital surgery, is assigned to a male prison in a protected section. Only 6 facilities have dedicated trans sections (including Rebibbia, Como, Belluno). A 2020 order of the Florence Supervisory Court ruled that legal sex should prevail, but in practice the DAP continues to rely on anatomy.

questions.text: Is hormone therapy for gender transition covered by the Italian National Health Service (SSN)?
options: No, it is entirely paid by the patient
Only in some regions
Yes, it has been free since 2020 thanks to two AIFA resolutions
Only below a certain income threshold
questions.explanation: Since 1 October 2020, AIFA resolutions 104272 and 104273 have made transition hormone medication free of charge (testosterone for trans men, estrogens and antiandrogens for trans women), upon diagnosis by a multidisciplinary team.

questions.text: What happens to an existing marriage when one of the spouses obtains legal gender recognition?
options: The marriage is automatically annulled
The marriage continues unchanged
If both wish, the marriage is converted into a civil union
The marriage is converted into a consensual separation
questions.explanation: The Cirinnà Law (76/2016) provides that, if both spouses declare they want to maintain the bond, the marriage automatically converts into a civil union. Otherwise it is dissolved. The Constitutional Court (ruling 170/2014) had declared automatic divorce without alternatives unconstitutional.

questions.text: The Zan Bill, which would have protected trans people from discrimination, was:
options: Approved in 2021
Rejected by the Chamber of Deputies in 2020
Blocked in the Senate by secret ballot in 2021
Withdrawn by its sponsor
questions.explanation: The Zan Bill was approved by the Chamber of Deputies in November 2020, but on 27 October 2021 the Senate killed it with the so-called "tagliola" guillotine motion (154 votes to 131), held by secret ballot. Italy remains without a national law explicitly protecting gender identity as a protected ground.

options: A national law allowing a name change without a court
A confidentiality agreement between a trans person and an institution to use their chosen name in internal documents
An alternative medical pathway to hormone therapy
A job reintegration program for trans people
questions.explanation: The alias career is an agreement between a trans person and an institution (school, university, employer) allowing the use of their chosen name in unofficial internal documents: badges, email, class registers. It is not based on a specific national law. To date about 475 Italian schools have adopted it, and the 2024 national school labor contract (art. 21) provides for it for school staff.

questions.text: Who can access data about the original sex at birth after legal recognition?
options: Anyone who requests it from the municipality
Employers and schools
Only the person concerned and law enforcement
No one, the data is deleted
questions.explanation: After rectification, public documents show only the new data. The full extract of the birth certificate (with the annotation) can only be requested by the person concerned. Law enforcement can access the previous data for security reasons. Gender identity is classified as sensitive data under the GDPR (art. 9).

questions.text: Does Legislative Decree 216/2003, the main anti-discrimination law in employment, explicitly protect gender identity?
options: Yes, both sexual orientation and gender identity
No, it covers only sexual orientation
Yes, since 2021
No, it covers neither
questions.explanation: Legislative Decree 216/2003, implementing EU Directive 2000/78, prohibits employment discrimination based on sexual orientation but does not explicitly mention gender identity. This gap would have been filled by the Zan Bill, never approved. Some regions (Tuscany, Piedmont, Liguria) have regional laws that include gender identity.

questions.text: Which Constitutional Court ruling removed the requirement of judicial authorization for gender-affirming surgery?
options: Ruling 221/2015
Ruling 170/2014
Ruling 143/2024
Ruling 180/2017
questions.explanation: Ruling 143/2024 declared unconstitutional the requirement of court authorization for surgery (art. 31, par. 4, Legislative Decree 150/2011), since transition can also occur without surgery, making it unreasonable to subject the operation to judicial approval.

questions.text: Is gender-affirming surgery covered by the Italian National Health Service?
options: No, it always has to be paid for
Yes, it is included in the LEA (Essential Levels of Care)
Only in accredited private facilities
Only for low-income adults
questions.explanation: Gender-affirming surgery is included in the LEA, the essential levels of care that the SSN must guarantee to all citizens. However, there are only about 7 specialized centers in Italy and waiting lists can be long.

levels.label: Beginner
levels.message: Italian legislation is complex, but it is important to know it. Read our articles in the Pathways section to learn more.

levels.label: Informed
levels.message: Good knowledge! There are still aspects to explore: take a look at our articles on rights and pathways.

levels.label: Expert
levels.message: Excellent command of Italian legislation. Share the quiz to make these rights known to more people!
